{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-wy-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"62456e8bf4109db5349ad91a363733e92f78588ef00cf6c3fa0777afd0bb60df","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-wy-class-c:lineage:62","source_registry_sha256":"f2806994ac56e29c3588fb4e8e2cc870c5f64d0616933994765d31d7841ccbe9","source_liveness_sha256":"e9e98c5695424e30c400f1e14b2593178d09ca723f8f00581c9655dcae32ca6c"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Hazards, work zones and driver attention — C2.01","heading":"C2 — Hazards, work zones and driver attention","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Hazards, work zones and driver attention
FACT_ID: sec14-R01 | anchor: A01
Recognize personal driving limitations and compensate for them or avoid driving while impaired. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec14-R02 | anchor: A01
Losing emotional self-control while driving increases errors and crash risk. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec14-R03 | anchor: A02
Do not drive when overwhelming emotion prevents self-control. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec14-R04 | anchor: A02
Strong grief, rage or terror can interfere with identifying hazards and making sound decisions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec14-R05 | anchor: A02
Even mild emotion can distract from driving, which requires full attention. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec14-R06 | anchor: A02
Clear vision helps identify critical objects early enough to predict, decide and respond. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec14-R07 | anchor: A02
Side vision helps detect objects entering from the sides. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec14-R08 | anchor: A02
Distance judgment supports driving decisions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec14-R09 | anchor: A02
Night vision and recovery after headlight glare are distinct parts of the source's good-vision description. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec14-R10 | anchor: A02
Glasses or contact lenses can compensate for difficulty seeing clearly. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec14-R11 | anchor: A02
A driver with poor side vision must move the head as well as the eyes and be especially careful with shoulder checks before lane changes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec14-R12 | anchor: A02
If a vision limitation cannot be adequately compensated, the source directs the person to stop driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec14-R13 | anchor: A03
Poor distance judgment calls for more following room and extra passing clearance. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-R14 | anchor: A03
The source connects poor distance judgment with difficulty predicting events 10 to 15 seconds ahead. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-R15 | anchor: A03
Slower night driving can compensate for poor night vision, but being 10 to 15 mph below other traffic may itself be hazardous. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-R16 | anchor: A03
The poor-night-vision guidance favors slower travel on well-lit streets or limiting driving to daylight. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-R17 | anchor: A03
When glare recovery is slow, looking toward the road's right side away from the glare can help. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-R18 | anchor: A03
For poor glare recovery, the handbook identifies daylight-only driving as the best solution. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-R19 | anchor: A03
Screeching tires, trains, sirens, horns or a motor in a blind spot can be auditory cues for changing speed or direction. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-R20 | anchor: A03
The handbook lists hearing aids and outside mirrors as ways to compensate for hearing loss. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-R21 | anchor: A03
Extra alertness, broader side scanning and side mirrors can help compensate for poor hearing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-R22 | anchor: A03
Even normal hearing may miss important road sounds when vehicle soundproofing or loud audio masks them. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-R23 | anchor: A03
Keep interior sound volume low enough to hear important traffic cues. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-R24 | anchor: A03
Using a cell phone while driving can distract from safe vehicle operation. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec14-R25 | anchor: A04
Conversation itself can be a major driving distraction, including during hands-free calls. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec14-R26 | anchor: A04
The handbook's Wyoming-law summary prohibits reading or sending text on a phone or other device while operating a vehicle. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec14-R27 | anchor: A04
Some Wyoming communities prohibit calls while operating a vehicle within city limits, so check local restrictions and posted notices. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec14-R28 | anchor: A04
WYDOT recommends pulling well off the highway and stopping before calling or texting. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec14-R29 | anchor: A04
Avoid long, emotional or otherwise distracting calls and arrange to call back when safe. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec14-R30 | anchor: A04
Decide to drive only when fully able, recognizing that physical, mental and emotional conditions can change daily. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec14-R31 | anchor: A04
A doctor's advice can help assess whether an illness or disability affects safe driving. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0089]
